cards.explanation: The answer is True. The LORD says, “I will sweep away man and beast; I will sweep away the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea, and the idols with their wicked worshipers.” (Zephaniah 1:3) The idols are named right there, and so are their wicked worshipers. So the statement is true, friends.

The word that fills the blank is priests. The LORD says He will cut off “…every remnant of Baal, the names of the idolatrous and pagan priests…” (Zephaniah 1:4) Baal is a false god, and the verse lists the remnant of Baal and then the names of those priests. So the blank is priests, friends.

The problem is that they also swear by Milcom. The LORD describes those “…who bow down and swear by the LORD but also swear by Milcom…” (Zephaniah 1:5) See that word "also"? These people swear by the LORD, but they swear by Milcom too. That's the problem right there, friends.

The answer is False. The verse says they are “…those who turn back from following the LORD, neither seeking the LORD nor inquiring of Him.” (Zephaniah 1:6) That "neither, nor" shuts the door on both. Turning back means they aren't seeking and they aren't inquiring.

The reason for the call to be silent is that the Day of the LORD is near. The verse says, “Be silent in the presence of the Lord GOD, for the Day of the LORD is near.” (Zephaniah 1:7) That "for" gives the reason, friends. The nearness of that day is why the call goes out.

The LORD names the princes and the sons of the king first. He says, “On the Day of the LORD’s sacrifice I will punish the princes, the sons of the king…” (Zephaniah 1:8) They're named first, before anyone else on the list, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says He will punish “…the princes, the sons of the king, and all who are dressed in foreign apparel.” (Zephaniah 1:8) After the princes and the sons of the king comes that next group. I looked down at my apron real quick, just to be safe.

They fill their master's house with violence and deceit. The LORD says He will punish “…all who leap over the threshold, who fill the house of their master with violence and deceit.” (Zephaniah 1:9) Those two words are what fills that house, friends. The verse names both of them plainly.

The dwellers of the Hollow are called to wail because their merchants will be silenced. The LORD says, “Wail, O dwellers of the Hollow, for all your merchants will be silenced; all who weigh out silver will be cut off.” (Zephaniah 1:11) The wailing comes with the silencing of the merchants. The verse also says all who weigh out silver will be cut off, friends.

What they say to themselves is that the LORD will do nothing, either good or bad. The LORD says He will punish “…the men settled in complacency, who say to themselves, ‘The LORD will do nothing, either good or bad.’” (Zephaniah 1:12) They figure He'll do nothing at all, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “They will build houses but not inhabit them, and plant vineyards but never drink their wine.” (Zephaniah 1:13) The building happens, but the living there doesn't, friends.

The answer is False. Verse 14 says, “Then the cry of the mighty will be bitter.” (Zephaniah 1:14) A bitter cry doesn't sound like someone standing strong and unshaken. Even the mighty are crying out on that day, friends.
A day of darkness and gloom is on the list. The LORD calls it “…a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness…” (Zephaniah 1:15) It's a heavy list, friends, line after line.

The answer is True. The LORD says that day is “…a day of horn blast and battle cry against the fortified cities, and against the high corner towers.” (Zephaniah 1:16) Even the cities built to be strong are named, friends.

The first blank is blind, and the second is sinned. The LORD says, “I will bring such distress on mankind that they will walk like the blind…” (Zephaniah 1:17) Notice that little word "like." The verse gives a comparison for how people will walk. Then the text states the reason itself: they will walk like the blind “…because they have sinned against the LORD.” (Zephaniah 1:17)

Their silver and gold won't be able to deliver them. The LORD says, “Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them on the Day of the LORD’s wrath.” (Zephaniah 1:18) Silver and gold are the two the verse names, friends, and neither one can deliver them on that day.
